_comment: Mutation testing. Coverage says a line RAN; a mutation score says a change to
that line FAILS something. The two diverge exactly where tests assert on spies
instead of behaviour, which the code-health audit measured at 1,091 spy-only
assertions concentrated in the orchestration files on the refactor list.
REPORT ONLY, NOT A GATE. `thresholds.break` is null on purpose: a score has no
meaning without a baseline, and runtime is O(mutants x suite). Read it before
restructuring a module, not on every push.
The package script uses pinned `pnpm dlx` packages so report-only tooling does
not enlarge every ordinary install, audit, or CI job.
`mutate` is deliberately NARROW -- the modules with characterization tests
written against them. Stryker's default would mutate the whole 218K-LOC tree
and run for hours. Override per investigation instead of widening this:
pnpm test:mutation --mutate 'src/some/other/file.ts'
`disableTypeChecks: false` matters more than it looks. Left at its default,
Stryker prepends `// @ts-nocheck` to EVERY file in the project before a run --
~1,500 files here -- and only restores them at the end, so an interrupted run
leaves the whole tree modified. Vitest transpiles through esbuild and never
type-checks, so stripping type errors buys nothing: the score is identical
either way (52.65% on input-handler.ts, measured both ways) while the files
touched drop from ~1,500 to the one being mutated.
Related hazard: an in-place run restores every file it backed up, so an edit
made WHILE a run is in flight is silently reverted when it finishes.
